statements.text: But at the same time is it not naive to think that we can make this voluntary indefinitely, that at some point there won't be a need for clarity in terms of what is demanded and expected from businesses in AI?
statements.context: House hearing on trustworthy AI where a congressman questions a NIST official about the future of the AI Risk Management Framework.

statements.text: I understand you're nonregulatory and ultimately it will come back to us and then come back to us just based on dangers. [...] It seems to me that we as human beings dramatically underestimate the potential for what artificial intelligence can bring humanity.
statements.context: Rep. Don Beyer questioning a witness during a House hearing on trustworthy AI and its risks.

statements.text: one of the things we pulled out of the President's executive order is the notion of mandating the NIST AI framework for Federal Government agencies using it, bill last week, bipartisan—Zach Nunn, Marcus Molinaro, Ted Lieu, and I—the Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act.
statements.context: US Representative Don Beyer speaking at a congressional forum on AI workforce readiness, discussing federal AI risk management legislation.

statements.text: Thank you very much. Dr. Toregas, the biggest thing that has come out of our AI Caucus so far is the Create AI Act, you know, creating a massive data set, not the 6 trillion words that Sam Altman scrubbed off the internet, but, rather, a curated data set for researchers and the like. Are we on the right track? Will this help us overcome some of the biases, the hallucinations, the incorrect information, or is it hopelessly naive?
statements.context: Rep. Don Beyer questions a witness during a congressional AI Caucus event on building an AI-ready workforce.

statements.text: Just last month, we introduced a bill called the AI Foundation Model Transparency Act to try to address the issue and shed some light into the black box of AI foundation models. My bill would call for the model deployer to make certain information about the training data, how the model is trained, publicly available. The hope is that users should know why the model is giving certain results, so it is not used in a discriminatory way.
statements.context: US Representative Don Beyer questioning an expert witness at a congressional hearing on building an AI-ready federal workforce.

statements.text: Now deepfakes are exacerbating these problems. Revenge porn wasn't a thing when I was in high school, but now AI allows anyone to create a pornographic image with the click of a button.
statements.context: House floor speech by Rep. Don Beyer on AI and mental health, delivered during a period of member statements on the topic.

statements.text: Colorado is trying to stop AI from discriminating in hiring.
statements.context: Remarks by Rep. Beyer during a hearing or markup on advancing America's AI Action Plan, discussing federal vs. state AI legislation.

statements.text: I noticed my colleague, George Whitesides, brought up the existential risk of artificial superintelligence before. [...] But let me move to a different thing. You know, we have this absence of meaningful AI legislation. [...] We're in this vast wasteland of nothing happening. [...] Mr. Kratsios, I'd love to be able to work with you on actually getting a Federal AI framework.
statements.context: House hearing on the Advancing America's AI Action Plan, featuring OSTP chief nominee Michael Kratsios.

statements.text: the President signed an Executive order that threatened States with lawsuits and the denial of billions of dollars of broadband supports if they adopted AI laws that were burdensome or onerous.
statements.context: Rep. Beyer questions an OSTP official during a congressional hearing on America's AI Action Plan, challenging the federal government's authority to override state AI laws.

statements.text: H.R. 8094. A bill to direct the Federal Trade Commission to establish requirements for making information available to the public about the training data and algorithms used in artificial intelligence foundation models, and for other purposes; to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.
statements.context: Introduction of public bills and resolutions on the House floor, where members file bill titles for committee referral.
